purpose.summary: Extend the passive mainnet harness to a fixed current-era checkpoint and require one exact joint-readiness observation before independent offline comparison.
scope: Start the exact baseline and candidate with fresh distinct datadirs before waiting, then require one joint-readiness observation where both processes are alive, RPC-ready, networkactive=true, localrelay=false and localaddresses is empty.
Let both roles independently acquire public mainnet blocks through fixed height 250000 under one shared 1800-second deadline and one shared two-GiB work-root cap.
Restart each role offline and compare genesis plus the immutable height-250000 block hash, raw header and chainwork.
Bind the exact expected checkpoint hash and median time, and require that the checkpoint median time is after the last legacy activation EMA time.

Retain bounded height overshoot, assumevalid=0, disabled wallet and authored-block or transaction surfaces, no inbound public service, closed RPC use, distinct processes, datadirs and eight ports, binary revalidation, sanitized reports and complete cleanup.
exclusions: No reproduction driver, workflow, container, dependency-lock, production-node, consensus, validation-rule, wallet, Chronik, activation, testnet, mainnet-parameter, cockpit, roadmap or evidence change.
No workflow dispatch, incoming artifact, evidence promotion or public-reproduction claim; the disclosed local same-binary mechanics smoke is not evidence.
No gettxoutsetinfo, rollback, reindex, corpus, authored transaction, block creation, relay injection or inbound public service.

No current-tip, full-history, global-mainnet-coexistence, sustained-operation, peer-diversity, concurrent-peer-connection, concurrent-public-traffic, minimum-overlap-duration, deterministic-build or operator-binary claim.
No raw child output, peer address, absolute host path, parent environment, cookie, secret, port, datadir or runtime artifact enters the report.
The existing reproduction driver remains bound to ERGON-CHANGE-0020; a later signed tooling packet must validate and bind this v3 target before any public dispatch.

limitations: The v3 profile has run locally only with distinct-inode copies of the same legacy executable; it has no candidate source-to-binary binding, public reconstruction or evidence artifact.
The fixed height-250000 checkpoint is current-era relative to the declared legacy activation boundary, but it does not cover the current tip or full history.
Joint readiness proves only one same-host observation in which both processes are alive, RPC-ready, networkactive=true, localrelay=false and localaddresses is empty.
Concurrent peer connections, concurrent public traffic and any minimum overlap duration are not established; distinct peers, network paths and hosts also remain open.
The shared 1800-second deadline and two-GiB work-root cap may yield an inconclusive result under slow or unavailable public acquisition.
The scenario does not establish sustained operation, operator-binary parity, deterministic builds or global mainnet coexistence.
The reproduction driver still validates the earlier v2 target and must be updated in a separate signed binding packet before this v3 harness can be dispatched.
counterevidence: No public reconstruction or workflow dispatch of the exact ERGON-CHANGE-0023 postimages exists at record-review time.

A local same-binary smoke used fresh distinct datadirs, processes and ports, observed joint readiness, acquired public blocks through checkpoint 250000, restarted both roles offline, matched the exact hash, header and chainwork, and removed every process and the work root; it validates harness mechanics but does not establish a candidate source-to-binary build binding or public reproduction.
Prior bounded checkpoint evidence does not answer whether both roles can validate through height 250000 or be jointly network-active under this v3 contract.
A same-host joint-readiness observation cannot demonstrate peer diversity, transport independence or deployment-wide mainnet coexistence.
Exact equality at one fixed checkpoint cannot establish current-tip agreement, complete historical replay or long-duration stability.
